Python is a great choice. Since you're totally new I would recommend Python and How to Think Like a Computer Scientist. There are some other free books, but I think that one is my favorite because it introduces some datastructures concepts towards the end.

I suggest using Ideone for fooling around, then using a compiler such as Clang for more serious works.

Here's a list from Wikipedia, but I recommend searching for individual people's opinions on whatever compiler before trying it out.
I tried those both extensively. I have a hard time judging whether those websites are any good because I haven't really learned a lot about programming. Is it that I'm just stupid?

Programming takes time to learn. It is not as easy as you think it is, and you can forget what commands you were supposed to learn. Keep going over it until you learn the commands and how the syntax of the language works.

If you already know Algebra or Physics then you know how formulas work, and can write a formula in almost any programming language. From that you learn how an algorithm works and how to write your own algorithms. From that you learn data structures and how to write your own data structures and from that you learn which ones are more effective and faster.

But you have to start out writing small programs first, Hello World, FizzBuzz, etc because it is like lifting weights. You can't start out lifting a 500 pound weight on your first day, so you start out with a 3 or 5 pound weight. You build that programming muscle and it takes years to do so.

This might be too simple to post here, I'm not sure, but everyone always dips strawberries in chocolate, so in addition to my super simple method of making this delicious snack, its a little PSA that choclate + orange = epic.

Ingredients:

2-3 of whatever variety of orange is available to you about 3-4 ounces of bittersweet chocolate (probably a lot more if you are like me). I find that semi-sweet is ok, but it really is best to go as dark as you can for this, the bitterness-tangyness contrast really kicks off this snack.

Directions:

  1. Melt chocolate in a microwave on half-power (or use a double boiler if you're old-fashioned like that).
  2. Cut the top and bottom off of the orange(s) so that it sits firmly on cutting board, then cut the peel off of the sides. I find that doing this makes the orange look really pretty and kind of professional looking, it takes off all the white part of the peel. Then cut the orange in half , and then into thin half-circle slices.
  3. Spread the orange slices out on a baking sheet (using wax paper, seran wrap, or foil if you like), and then using a spoon put small dollops of the melted chocolate on top. It has just occurred to me that if you dip the slices in the chocolate, it might look nicer, try it out.
  4. Stick baking sheet in freezer until chocolate sets. I normally can't wait longer than 15 minutes.
  5. Enjoy!

Here's something to do do with the left-over peels. Israeli Chocolate-Coated Orange Peels.

It may be an acquired taste for some, but you are half way there!
